In this repository (working dir /bench/repo), there is a concept of a "memo" (note/document). Each memo carries DERIVED metadata that is computed from its content rather than set by the user — used for lists/previews (e.g. title, preview/excerpt, word count, etc.).

Find:
1. The exact file path and function/site where this derived metadata is COMPUTED from memo content.
2. Which operations TRIGGER recomputation (e.g. create, update, save).
3. What PROPERTIES the computation extracts.

Search for terms like "memo", "metadata", "preview", "excerpt", "deriveMetadata", "computeMetadata", "title", "wordCount", etc. Report exact file paths with line numbers and quote the relevant code. Be thorough — look at models, schemas, ORM hooks, services.

content.text:
I have a complete picture. This is the `usememos/memos` codebase (Go backend). Here is what I found.

## Summary

Derived memo metadata is computed by a markdown service using goldmark AST parsing. There are two categories: **persisted** metadata (stored in the memo's `Payload`) and **on-the-fly** metadata (the snippet, computed at read time).

## 1. Where the computation happens

**Persisted metadata — computation entry point:**
`/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74` — `RebuildMemoPayload(...)`

```go
func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
	if memo.Payload == nil {
		memo.Payload = &storepb.MemoPayload{}
	}
	// Use goldmark service to extract all metadata in a single pass (more efficient)
	data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
	...
	memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
	memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
	return nil
}
```

**The actual extraction logic** (single-pass AST walk):
`/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go:356` — `(*service).ExtractAll(content []byte)`. This walks the goldmark AST and populates `ExtractedData{Tags, Mentions, Property}`. Related single-purpose methods live in the same file: `ExtractTags` (line 143), `ExtractProperties` (line 193), and `GenerateSnippet` (line 264).

**On-the-fly metadata (snippet/excerpt)** is NOT stored. It is generated each time a memo is converted to an API response:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76-80` calls `getMemoContentSnippet(memo.Content)` and sets `memoMessage.Snippet`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83` — `getMemoContentSnippet` calls `s.MarkdownService.GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)` (max 64 chars).

## 2. What triggers recomputation

`RebuildMemoPayload` is invoked from these sites (there is no ORM/store-level hook — it is explicitly called in the service layer before persisting):

- **Create memo:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` — always called on create.
- **Update memo (content change):** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447` — only when the `UpdateMask` includes the `"content"` path (line 436). The recomputed `memo.Payload` is then assigned to `update.Payload` (line 451). Other update paths (visibility, pinned, location, etc.) do NOT trigger recomputation.
- **Bulk backfill runner:** `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52` — `RunOnce` rebuilds the payload for all memos in batches of 100 and persists each via `Store.UpdateMemo` (line 56).

Note: `Payload.Location` (line 112 on create, line 483 on update for the `"location"` path) is set from user input, not derived — it is not part of the content-derived computation.

The **snippet** is recomputed on every read/conversion (converter line 76), so it has no explicit trigger — it is always fresh.

## 3. Properties extracted

**Persisted in `MemoPayload`** (proto: `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto:7-29`):
- `tags` (`[]string`) — deduplicated `#tags`, case preserved (`markdown.go:376-378, 418`).
- `property` — a `MemoPayload_Property` message with:
  - `title` (string) — text of the first H1 heading, only if it is the first block-level node (`markdown.go:384-389`).
  - `has_link` (bool) — content contains a link (`markdown.go:393-394`).
  - `has_code` (bool) — content has a code block, fenced code block, or code span (`markdown.go:396-397`).
  - `has_task_list` (bool) — content has a task checkbox (`markdown.go:399-400`).
  - `has_incomplete_tasks` (bool) — has at least one unchecked task (`markdown.go:401-404`).

  (`ExtractAll` also computes `Mentions` — lowercased `@usernames`, `markdown.go:379-381` — but `RebuildMemoPayload` only copies `Tags` and `Property` into the payload; mentions are used elsewhere.)

**Computed on the fly (not stored):**
- `Snippet` — plain-text excerpt/preview, max 64 chars, truncated at a word boundary with `" ..."` suffix; skips code blocks, joins block elements with spaces (`GenerateSnippet`, `markdown.go:264-346`; `truncateAtWord`, line 472).

I did not find a separate `wordCount` field — it is not computed or stored anywhere in this codebase; the preview equivalent is the `Snippet`.
